proposals.Name: cached_prefix_frontier
proposals.Title: Prefix Caching Moves the Break-Even: Measured Accuracy–GPU-Second Frontiers for Static, Whole-Bank and Retrieved Experience Prefixes in a Multi-Turn Agent
proposals.Short Hypothesis: In a multi-turn agent served with prefix caching, the cost of an experience prefix is set by how many distinct prefixes the arm emits across episodes and by how long the prefix is at decode time, not by its injected token count, so a matched-token budget mis-ranks the routes. Concretely: with caching off, an 80-item whole-bank prefix (~11k tokens) costs at least 3x the GPU-seconds per episode of k=3 retrieval (~430 tokens); with caching on it costs at most 1.5x, and k=3 retrieval costs at most 25% more than a type-conditioned static prompt because only the first turn's retrieved tokens are uncached. Retrieval from a small bank (24 or 80 items) keeps the accuracy of retrieval from the full 1,465-item bank while emitting few distinct prefixes, so retrieval's accuracy is available at static cost.
proposals.Related Work: 2603.04814 builds a cost model with prompt caching for Mem0 versus long context on conversational QA with one model; cost is modelled per turn, never measured inside an agent loop, and there is no compiled-static or whole-bank arm. AdaptiveScale (s2:62b577ec) and KVFlow (2507.07400) treat prefix-cache hit rate as a serving quantity with no task accuracy attached. InferScale (2607.27090) and HYPIC (2607.01299) make injected memory position-independently cacheable, engineering whose payoff is exactly the retrieval premium this idea measures. 2607.26497 finds retrieval crossovers on document corpora with one reader and no cost under caching; 2506.04301 reports agent compute scaling without a memory axis; Preping (2605.13880) claims 2-3x lower deployment cost for pre-built playbooks without separating caching from content; 2604.02596 shows BM25-selected shots beat many-shot on data efficiency in MT, not on serving cost. Archived memory_budget_confound (5.63) matched token budgets and treated tokens as the cost axis.
proposals.Abstract: Agent-memory papers count injected tokens as the cost of retrieval and treat a static prompt as free once cached; neither is what a serving stack charges. In a multi-turn agent every decode step re-reads the prefix through attention, a cached prefix still occupies KV memory that bounds batch size, and only the first turn of a retrieved prefix is uncached. We measure, rather than model, accuracy–GPU-second frontiers on ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B for three routes built from the same expert bank: compiled static prompts (type-agnostic and type-conditioned), the whole bank in context (24 and 80 items), and top-k retrieval from banks of 24, 80, 240 and 1,465 items. Each arm runs with vLLM prefix caching on and off on the same 274 games x 2 seeds as Measurements A and C, at a concurrency tuned to the serving queue on two A100s, with per-request uncached prefill, decode tokens and per-turn context length logged. We fit a three-term cost model (uncached prefill, decode tokens, decode x context length) and test it on a held-out arm. The predictions: caching reverses the cost ranking of whole-bank versus retrieval; the retrieval premium over a static prompt under caching is a first-turn effect below 25%; and retrieval from a small bank matches the full bank's accuracy while emitting few distinct prefixes. The output is a Pareto set per cache setting and a portable token-level accounting that replaces matched-token budgets.
proposals.Experiments: E0 (on disk, reused): Measurement A arms k=0, k=3, k=7 and Measurement C arms (type-conditioned 3 fixed exemplars; type-agnostic 6-procedure prompt) give accuracy on 274 games x 2 seeds. E1 new accuracy arms, 274 x 2 each: whole-bank-24 (4 items per type, ~3.4k tokens, one prefix), whole-bank-80 (13-14 per type, ~11k tokens, one prefix; truncation rule: stratified by type, shortest successful trajectories first), and BM25 goal retrieval k=3 from random type-stratified bank subsets of 24, 80 and 240 items; 2,740 episodes (~2.5 h). E2 cost runs: all nine arms x prefix caching {on, off} x ~270 episodes, arms interleaved in 3 blocks of 90 episodes, both GPUs, workers raised until each replica's running queue is at least 8; log per request prompt_tokens, cached_tokens, completion_tokens and per-turn context length from the vLLM usage fields, wall-clock per block and nvidia-smi utilization every 10 s; GPU-seconds per episode = 2 x wall-clock / episodes at saturated queue; 4,860 episodes (~4 h). E3 fit GPU-s = a x uncached_prefill + b x decode_tokens + c x sum over decode steps of context length on eight arms and predict the ninth (whole-bank-24). E4 frontier: success from E0/E1 against GPU-s per episode from E2 for both routes under both cache settings; Pareto set per setting; additional concurrency ladder (8/16/32 workers per replica) on whole-bank-80 and k=3, cost only, to expose KV-occupancy effects. Positive controls: (i) the caching toggle must cut the type-agnostic static arm's uncached prefill tokens by at least 5x, otherwise the cache is not functioning and no cost claim is made; (ii) k=3 accuracy under cache on versus off must agree within the ±8 floor, otherwise cost and accuracy cannot be paired.
proposals.Baselines and Ablations: Baselines (static arms first, per the brief): k=0; type-agnostic 6-procedure prompt (1 distinct prefix); type-conditioned 3 fixed exemplars (6 distinct prefixes); whole-bank-24 and whole-bank-80 (1 prefix each). Retrieval route: BM25 goal retrieval k=3 from 24, 80, 240 and 1,465 items (distinct prefixes rising toward C(n_type,3)); k=7 from 1,465. Ablations: caching on/off (cost only); concurrency 8/16/32 per replica (cost only); retrieved items ordered canonically by item id so identical sets share a prefix versus ordered by score (cost only); whole-bank-80 item order type-blocked versus shuffled (accuracy, exploratory).
proposals.Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (headline, cost-ranking reversal): with caching off, whole-bank-80 costs at least 3x the GPU-s per episode of k=3 retrieval; with caching on, at most 1.5x. Falsified by whole-bank-80 at or above 2x k=3 with caching on (decode attention over an 11k context and KV occupancy dominate, or the shared prefix is evicted under concurrency), produced by the whole-bank-80 versus k=3 cells of E2 under cache on; or by a cache-off ratio below 2, produced by the same pair under cache off. P2: with caching on, k=3 retrieval costs at most 25% more GPU-s per episode than the type-conditioned 3-exemplar static arm. Falsified by a premium at or above 50%, produced by the k=3 versus 3-fixed-exemplar cells under cache on (first-turn prefill dominance or per-turn cache misses would produce it). P3: whole-bank-80 success is within ±8 net of k=3 retrieval on both splits. Falsified by whole-bank-80 at least 8 net below k=3 (many-shot distraction), produced by the whole-bank-80 arm of E1; not entailed, since containing the items does not make the reader use them. P4: retrieval-from-24 and retrieval-from-80 are within ±8 net of retrieval-from-1,465 while their uncached prefill tokens under caching are at most 30% of the full-bank arm's. Falsified by success at least 8 net lower at 24 or 80 (item specificity matters), produced by the bank-size ladder of E1; or by a cache-hit fraction at or below 50% at bank 24 (prefix diversity from set/order variation), produced by that arm's cached_tokens logs. P5: the three-term cost model predicts the held-out whole-bank-24 arm's GPU-s per episode within 25%. Falsified by held-out error above 25%, produced by E3.
proposals.Measurement and Noise Control: Accuracy: paired (game, seed) cells with A and C on 274 x 2; ±8 net floor for arm-versus-arm claims; margins stated as fractions of the Gate-0 gain (+27/+32 net at k=3): the ±8 in P3/P4 is 25-30% of that gain; per-type numbers exploratory. Cost: GPU-s per episode from wall-clock at saturated queue in 3 interleaved blocks per arm per cache setting, median and bootstrap CI over blocks; token quantities from per-request vLLM usage fields; utilization and throughput (episodes/min, tok/s per GPU) reported per arm; ratios in P1/P2 computed on block medians with CIs from 1,000 bootstrap resamples of episodes, and a prediction counts as confirmed only if its CI excludes the falsifying value. Cost-model fit reports R-squared and held-out error. Pre-registration of arms, truncation rule, concurrency and floors before E1.
proposals.Preprint Collision Check: home: 'prefix caching KV cache reuse shared prefix multi-turn inference cost long system prompt' (--recent; channel s2+hf): UltraQuant 2606.20474, KVTC 2511.01815, KVCOMM 2510.12872, KVFlow 2507.07400, KVShare 2503.16525; all serving-systems papers, none pairs cache hit rate with task accuracy of static versus retrieved prefixes. Closest method: 'memory system versus long context accuracy cost break-even prompt caching agent' (--recent; s2+hf): 2603.04814 (modelled caching cost, conversational QA, no agent loop, no whole-bank or compiled arm), InferScale 2607.27090 (KV injection replacing prefill of memory facts; verified via paper lookup, s2), HYPIC 2607.01299, Harness the Memory 2608.15008 (memory substrates, regime-dependent, verified via paper lookup, hf), 2607.12893, 2606.18829, 2604.20006, 2605.12493. 'many-shot in-context learning whole example bank in context versus retrieved top-k examples cost accuracy' (--recent; s2+hf): no results. 'many-shot in-context learning versus retrieval augmented examples' (--recent; s2+hf): 2604.02596 (many-shot MT, BM25 retrieval improves data efficiency, no serving cost), 2506.04579, 2502.09933, 2501.10834. No paper measures a cache-toggle cost reversal between whole-bank and retrieved prefixes in an agent loop.
proposals.Risk Factors and Limitations: KV memory on an 80GB A100 with a 32B reader may evict the 11k shared prefix under high concurrency, turning the whole-bank arm into an uncached arm; this is a real outcome (it falsifies P1) but node-specific, so the KV budget and the concurrency at which eviction starts are reported. vLLM prefix caching is position-dependent; item-level position-independent KV reuse (InferScale-style) would shrink the retrieval premium further and is stated as the implication, not measured. GPU-seconds depend on the serving stack; the token-level accounting is portable, the fitted coefficients are not. ALFWorld's 140-token items let 80 fit in 16k; environments with 1k-token items hit the whole-bank ceiling at 16 items. One reader; the crossover-moves-with-reader question is left to a second backbone.
proposals.Addresses gap: G25 (accuracy-cost curves under prompt caching untested) and G21 (no same-budget whole-bank control).
proposals.Not a restatement of: Brief bullet 'Cost: a static prefix is prefix-cached by vLLM; retrieval injects a different prefix per episode, so the token cost difference is measurable': the brief treats injected token count as the cost; this idea claims token counts mis-rank the routes because a cached prefix is still paid at every decode step and occupies KV, and it manipulates caching to show the ranking reversal. Nearest digest card 2603.04814: models caching cost for single-turn QA; this idea claims the agent loop changes the accounting (only first-turn retrieved tokens are uncached, the static prefix is paid at decode) and measures it with whole-bank and compiled arms. Archived memory_budget_confound (5.63): matched token budgets; this idea claims matched tokens is the wrong cost axis under caching.

proposals.Name: exemplar_lottery
proposals.Title: The Exemplar Lottery: Retrieval's Gain Over a Fixed Prompt Is a Quantile of the Static Arm's Draw Distribution, Not a Mean Shift
proposals.Short Hypothesis: A fixed exemplar prompt is one draw from the bank, and reported retrieval gains are measured against a single draw. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B, the success of a type-conditioned three-exemplar fixed prompt varies across random draws from the same expert bank by more than the mean gap between retrieval and the fixed arm; retrieval sits at the upper quantile of that draw distribution, does not beat the best held-out draw by more than the noise floor, and a one-time length rule (shortest successful trajectories per type) recovers it without a query. Retrieval's value on a template environment is selection robustness, and it has to be reported against the draw distribution with its spread.
proposals.Related Work: Traj-Bootstrap (2505.00234, NeurIPS 2025) grows a self-generated example database on ALFWorld and other tasks, notices that equal-size databases differ in quality, and picks the best by population-based selection plus exemplar-level curation; it always retrieves and never compares to a fixed no-retriever draw, so the variance it exploits is never attributed to exemplar choice versus retrieval. Classic ICL sensitivity work (calibrate-before-use, prompt-order sensitivity, kNN demonstration selection beating random) measured the spread of random demonstration draws on classification and showed retrieval beats the random mean, not the random maximum or a curated fixed set, and never on multi-turn agent trajectories. 2512.04106 (retrieved few-shot beats random few-shot on vulnerability detection, one model, no curated fixed set) and 2406.14596 ICAL (retrieved insight exemplars, no fixed-set test) report one static comparison each. SkillEvolBench (2605.24117) calls skill gains unstable without decomposing the instability. Measurement C on this node runs one draw per static arm. Archived decorative_retriever (5.75) observed retrieval-set overlap.
proposals.Abstract: Every static exemplar prompt is a draw from the bank, and the reported gain of retrieval over it is measured against one draw. We ask what the distribution of that draw looks like and where retrieval sits in it. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B we run 16 random draws of a type-conditioned three-exemplar prompt from the expert bank, 8 draws from the self pool, and, for 8 random 80-item bank samples, both a fixed draw and k=3 retrieval from the same sample, all paired on the 274 games x 2 seeds of Measurement A; we add three one-time curation rules (shortest trajectories, retriever-embedding medoids, longest trajectories) that select exemplars without a query. We decompose the fixed arm's variance into draw, seed and game components and locate retrieval's success in the draw distribution, selecting the best draw on a held-out split to avoid the winner's curse. The claim is that retrieval's gain over a fixed prompt on a template environment is the spread of the exemplar lottery, not a mean shift. If instead the draws cluster and retrieval exceeds the best held-out draw by more than the floor, retrieval carries per-instance information that no fixed prompt has. Either outcome fixes how retrieval gains should be reported: against the draw distribution, with its spread, and with the cheapest curation rule as the static arm.
proposals.Experiments: E0 (on disk): A (k=0; k=3 BM25 retrieval from the full expert bank, R_full) and C (one fixed draw, reported later as its quantile in the lottery). E1: F_1..F_16, type-conditioned fixed prompts, each a uniform draw of 3 successful expert trajectories per type from the full bank, same slot and format as C's fixed arm, token-matched to k=3 (~430 tokens); 274 x 2 each, 8,768 episodes (~7.3 h). E2: S_1..S_8, the same from the self pool (on-policy detours); 4,384 episodes (~3.7 h). E3: 8 random type-stratified 80-item bank samples; for each, F_b (fixed draw of 3 per type from the sample) and R_b (k=3 BM25 retrieval from the sample), paired; 8,768 episodes (~7.3 h). E4: curation arms C_short (3 shortest successful trajectories per type), C_medoid (per-type medoids under the retriever's own representation), C_worst (3 longest per type, negative control); 1,644 episodes (~1.4 h). E5: held-out best-draw selection: choose the best of F_1..16 on seed 1 x valid_seen and compare to R_full on seed 2 x valid_unseen, and the mirror. E6: variance decomposition: crossed random-effects logistic model with game, draw and draw x seed intercepts; simple SDs of arm-level net scores across draws and across seeds reported alongside; bootstrap over games. Static arms are prefix-cached and retrieval arms are not; uncached prefill tokens per episode logged for every arm as a secondary cost axis. Total ~23.6k episodes (~20 h on two A100s), pre-registered draw seeds.
proposals.Baselines and Ablations: Baselines: k=0; R_full (retrieval k=3 from 1,465 items); the 16 expert draws and 8 self-pool draws as the static-arm distribution; the 8 paired (F_b, R_b) bank samples; C's single draw located as a quantile. Curation arms as one-time static alternatives: C_short, C_medoid, C_worst. Ablations: draws restricted to scene-disjoint items for each test game (removes near-duplicate luck from the lottery); single-exemplar draws token-matched to k=1 for 8 draws if budget allows; the self-pool draws with detour steps removed by rule (tests whether the wider spread, if found, is from detours or from selection).
proposals.Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (headline): the SD across the 16 expert draws of net success is at least 2x the within-draw seed SD, and the draw range (max minus min) is at least the mean gap R_full minus mean(F_d). Falsified by draw SD at or below seed SD, or a range below half the mean gap, produced by the F_1..16 arm if draws cluster (a live outcome, since expert trajectories within a type share the procedure). P2: R_full does not exceed the held-out best draw by more than 8 net. Falsified by R_full minus F_best-heldout above 8 net (retrieval carries per-instance information beyond exemplar choice), produced by E5. P3: self-pool draws have SD at least 1.5x the expert draws' SD and a mean at least 8 net lower. Falsified by SD_self at or below SD_expert, produced by E2 (self-pool successes are procedurally equivalent despite detours). P4: C_short lands within ±8 net of R_full and C_worst lands at least 8 net below R_full. Falsified by C_short at least 8 net below R_full (a cheap rule does not recover retrieval's selection), produced by E4; or by C_worst within ±8 of R_full (exemplar choice does not matter, which also removes P1's premise), produced by E4. P5: over the 8 bank samples the paired residual R_b minus F_b has mean within ±8 net and an across-sample SD larger than its across-seed SD. Falsified by a mean residual above 8 net (retrieval beats a same-bank fixed draw on average), produced by E3.
proposals.Measurement and Noise Control: All arms on the 274 x 2 (game, seed) grid of A, so every comparison is paired; ±8 net floor for arm-versus-arm claims and margins of 25-30% of the Gate-0 gain (+27/+32). Draw SD is estimated over 16 arm-level net scores, each on 548 episodes (per-draw SE about 2 net), so a draw SD of 4 net is distinguishable from the seed SD estimated from the 16 paired seed differences; the chi-square CI on an SD from 16 draws is about ±35%, hence the 2x ratio in P1. Range and quantile statements carry bootstrap CIs from 1,000 resamples of games drawn jointly across arms to preserve pairing. The held-out selection in E5 removes the winner's curse from best-draw comparisons. Per-type spreads are exploratory. Pre-registration lists draw seeds, bank-sample seeds, curation rules and floors before any run.
proposals.Preprint Collision Check: home: 'in-context example selection sensitivity to demonstration choice random demonstrations variance fixed demonstration set versus retrieved' (no recency; channel s2+hf): 2506.04579 gradient-matching many-shot selection, 2603.26775 RL visual demonstration selection, 2309.07900 ambiguity-aware ICL, 2406.10229 variance in evaluation benchmarks, 2304.01910 calibrated chaos; none locates retrieval in the draw distribution of a fixed set. Mechanism, last twelve months: 'demonstration selection robustness variance across example draws kNN selection versus best fixed set' (--recent; s2+hf): 2606.27997 dataset selection for rankings, 2512.08956 DW-KNN; nothing relevant. 'in-context trajectory examples sensitivity example choice agent variance seeds' (--recent; s2+hf): 2607.08716, 2601.07058, 2607.22682; nothing relevant. Closest method: 'WebShop ALFWorld trajectory retrieval exemplars experience memory static prompt comparison' (--recent; s2+hf): Traj-Bootstrap 2505.00234 (verified via paper lookup, s2, NeurIPS 2025, 19 citations; database-level selection exploits DB-to-DB variance under retrieval, no fixed no-retriever draw), 2605.16986 Skills on the Fly, 2604.20572 ProactAgent, 2607.10608, 2605.29463, 2605.12493, 2608.20707. No paper reports the draw distribution of a fixed agent exemplar prompt or retrieval's quantile within it.
proposals.Risk Factors and Limitations: The expert pool's within-type homogeneity may make the lottery narrow, in which case P1 fails and the honest result is that a fixed prompt is robust to the draw on ALFWorld and the retrieval residual is a genuine (small or null) mean shift; the self pool and C_worst provide the positive control for exemplar sensitivity, and if C_worst also matches R_full the environment cannot discriminate exemplar quality and the claim is confined to the self pool. Sixteen draws give a wide CI on the SD; only ratios at or above 2 are conclusive. One retriever (BM25 on goal), one reader, one environment; a WebShop replication is a follow-up. The variance model treats draws as exchangeable; near-duplicate luck is handled by the scene-disjoint ablation. About 20 GPU-hours.
proposals.Addresses gap: G24 (run-to-run and selection variance of memory gains unreported) and G22 (no random or fixed selection control at matched prompt length).
proposals.Not a restatement of: Brief bullet 'Measurement C: one fixed expert exemplar / three fixed exemplars token-matched': C runs one draw per static arm and cannot tell whether that draw was lucky; this idea manipulates the draw (16 expert draws, 8 self-pool draws, 8 paired bank samples) and claims the retrieval-minus-static gap is a quantile of the draw distribution rather than a mean shift, recoverable by a one-time length rule. Nearest digest card 2505.00234 (Traj-Bootstrap): it observes database-to-database variance under retrieval and selects the best database; this idea claims the variance lives in the static arm's exemplar choice, that retrieval equals the upper quantile of a no-retriever lottery, and that curation without a query matches it. Archived decorative_retriever (5.75) observed overlap; this idea manipulates draws and bank samples and decomposes variance.

proposals.Name: recall_success_dissociation
proposals.Title: Recall Ranks Retrievers, Success Does Not: A Two-Environment Audit of Experience Retrieval Against the Static Prompt with Manipulated Duplicate Availability
proposals.Short Hypothesis: Retriever recall (fraction of top-k items sharing the test task's type or binding) and the task-success residual over the best static prompt dissociate, and the dissociation is set by whether the retrieved binding is recoverable inside the episode. On ALFWorld, the residual over the best static arm is a step at type recall (random-type retrieval loses, BM25 and an oracle same-scene retriever sit within the floor) and is unchanged when same-scene items are removed from the bank, because object locations are recoverable by looking; on WebShop, where the binding (which product satisfies the attribute set) is expensive to recover by search, the residual appears only when a same-product trajectory is in the bank and tracks product recall. Recall above the type threshold is therefore uninformative unless the bank carries non-recoverable bindings, and retriever evaluation must report success residual over the static arm at two duplicate-availability levels.
proposals.Related Work: 2604.04949 trains retrievers from agent trajectories and reports evidence recall and task success together with no random or fixed control, so recall and success are never dissociated. 2512.20854 correlates retrieval metrics with LLM-judged answer quality in RAG QA and 2508.05909 tries to isolate the retriever's contribution to a reader; both are single-turn QA with no static arm. 2603.02473 finds retrieval dominates write strategy on LoCoMo (QA, no full-history or fixed arm). SWE-ContextBench (2602.08316) shows correctly selected related-task experience helps and mis-selected experience harms on dependency-linked tasks, without a random or static control; 2607.10608 shows wrong retrieved memory is adopted at the first decision point. Traj-Bootstrap (2505.00234) and ExpeL/Reflexion report ALFWorld and WebShop memory gains over no memory only. Measurement A on this node observed unseen approximately equal to seen with one retriever and no static arm. Archived decorative_retriever (5.75) observed retrieval-set overlap without manipulating it.
proposals.Abstract: Retrievers for agent memory are ranked by recall of relevant items; whether that ranking survives when the outcome is task success over the best static prompt is unknown, and it should depend on whether the retrieved item carries something the agent cannot recover in the episode. We manipulate two things on two environments: retriever recall (random-type, goal-BM25, oracle same-binding, at matched k=3) and the bank's duplicate availability (with versus without items sharing the test task's binding: scene on ALFWorld, goal product on WebShop). Every retrieval cell is reported as the success residual over the best static arm built from the same bank (fixed exemplars, compiled procedure, whole bank where it fits), paired on games and seeds, with Qwen3-32B. The prediction is a dissociation: on ALFWorld the residual is a step at type recall and flat above it, unaffected by removing same-scene items; on WebShop the residual appears only when a same-product trajectory is in the bank and tracks product recall, and vanishes when duplicates are removed. A positive control (retrieval over no memory clearing the floor on WebShop) gates the second environment. The audit yields a rule for evaluating experience retrievers: report success residual over the static arm under two duplicate-availability levels, and treat recall above the type threshold as uninformative unless the bank carries bindings the episode cannot recover.
proposals.Experiments: E0 ALFWorld reuse: A (k=0; BM25 k=3) and C (static arms; the best static arm chosen on pooled cells). E1 ALFWorld retriever ladder at k=3, 274 x 2 each: random-type (uniform over the bank, type recall about 1/6), goal-BM25 (A, type recall about 1), oracle same-type-same-scene on valid_seen (binding recall 1; on valid_unseen it reduces to same-type); C's different-type placebo serves as the recall-0 point; 1,644 episodes (~1.5 h). E2 ALFWorld duplicate manipulation: BM25 k=3 with a per-game bank filter excluding same-scene items on valid_seen, paired with A's k=3; 548 episodes. E3 WebShop setup (one day) and bank: Qwen3-32B run on 3,000 train instructions at k=0; successes form bank-full; per test instruction, bank-dup (full) and bank-nodup (items whose goal product equals the test goal product removed); achieved same-product rates reported (target at least 30% versus 0%); the public human demonstrations are added if the self-success rate is thin. E4 WebShop arms, 500 test instructions x 2 seeds each: k=0; static arms: fixed 3 exemplars (token-matched to k=3), compiled procedure (~80 tokens, written by rule from the bank), whole-bank-in-context up to 16k with shortest-first truncation; retrieval k=3: random, instruction-BM25, oracle same-product, each under bank-dup and bank-nodup (cells that coincide are shared); about 10.5k episodes (~8 h). E5 gate: WebShop BM25 k=3 over k=0 must clear the floor before any residual claim. E6 analysis: for each retriever and bank level, recall@3 (type or category recall; binding recall = same scene or same product) and success residual over the best static arm at that bank level; residual plotted against binding recall for both environments; residual per uncached prefill token reported as the cost axis.
proposals.Baselines and Ablations: Baselines (static arms first, per the brief): k=0; fixed 3 exemplars token-matched to k=3; compiled procedure prompt; whole-bank-in-context where it fits; on ALFWorld the C arms including the type-agnostic 6-procedure prompt. Manipulations: retriever ladder (random-type, BM25, oracle same-binding) and bank duplicate availability (dup versus nodup) on both environments. Ablations: k=1 versions of oracle and BM25 on WebShop (residual is not a length effect); type-agnostic procedure-only static on WebShop versus fixed exemplars; random-type retrieval on WebShop with bank-dup (isolates the item content from the binding).
proposals.Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (ALFWorld step): the residual over the best static arm is at or below minus 8 net for random-type retrieval and within ±8 for BM25 and oracle same-scene. Falsified by an oracle residual above 8 net (scene bindings carry value that the static arm lacks), produced by the oracle arm on valid_seen; or by random-type retrieval within ±8 of the static arm (procedures do not matter, contradicting A), produced by the random-type arm. P2 (ALFWorld manipulation): excluding same-scene items changes the BM25 k=3 residual by less than 8 net. Falsified by a drop of at least 8 net, produced by E2. P3 (WebShop manipulation): under bank-nodup every retriever's residual over the best static arm is within the floor; under bank-dup, oracle same-product and BM25 residuals are at least 8 net with oracle at or above BM25. Falsified by a residual of at least 8 net under bank-nodup (retrieval carries value beyond duplicates, for example category search strategies), produced by the bank-nodup BM25 or oracle arm; or by oracle same-product within the floor under bank-dup (a duplicate trajectory does not transfer the binding), produced by the bank-dup oracle arm. P4 (cross-environment): the slope of residual on binding recall is within the floor on ALFWorld and at least 8 net per unit recall on WebShop under bank-dup. Falsified by same-sign slopes of the same size on both environments, produced by the two ladders jointly. P5 (gate, positive control): WebShop BM25 k=3 beats k=0 by at least the WebShop floor. If falsified, produced by E5, the WebShop side is declared uninformative and P3/P4 are not claimed.
proposals.Measurement and Noise Control: ALFWorld: paired (game, seed) cells with A and C on 274 x 2, ±8 net floor; the best static arm is chosen on pooled cells across both splits so no per-split winner is selected; margins as fractions of the Gate-0 gain (+27/+32). WebShop: 500 x 2 paired cells; the floor is estimated from two independent k=0 replicates with different seed pairs before any claim (expected about ±6 net) and the larger of that estimate and ±8 is used; success (score = 1) primary, WebShop score secondary; residuals with bootstrap CIs over instructions (1,000 resamples, jointly across arms). Recall computed per episode from retrieved item ids. Per-category WebShop and per-type ALFWorld results exploratory. proposals.Risk Factors and Limitations: WebShop install plus bank generation is a day and about two GPU-hours; if Qwen3-32B's WebShop success is low, the bank is thin and the same-product rate under bank-dup may be small, with the public human demonstrations as the fallback. WebShop's graded score is reported as secondary; the success dichotomy drives the floor. The oracle same-scene retriever exists only on valid_seen. Two environments are two points; the rule is a prediction to test on a third. The WebShop whole-bank arm is truncated (items are longer) and reported with its truncation rule. If P5 fails, the cross-environment claim is not made and the ALFWorld step result stands alone.
